title: The concept of rational numbers
competency: Describe rational numbers practically and express them as fractions.

keywords.def: A number that can be written as a/b, where a and b are integers and b ≠ 0.
The whole numbers and their opposites: …, −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, …

en.text: You know natural numbers, whole numbers and integers. A rational number is any number you can write as a fraction a/b of two integers, with b not zero. 22 Birr shared by 5 pets gives 22/5 Birr each. That is a rational number.

am.text: የተፈጥሮ ቁጥሮችን፣ ሙሉ ቁጥሮችንና ኢንቲጀሮችን ታውቃለህ። ሬሽናል ቁጥር በሁለት ኢንቲጀሮች ክፍልፋይ a/b ሊጻፍ የሚችል ቁጥር ነው፤ b ዜሮ መሆን የለበትም። 22 ብር ለ5 የቤት እንስሳት ሲካፈል እያንዳንዱ 22/5 ብር ያገኛል።

screens.ask: Solomon has 3 cats and 2 dogs. He has 22 Birr for toys. How much can he spend on each pet?
screens.after:
There are 3 + 2 = 5 pets.
22 ÷ 5 = 4 remainder 2, so each pet gets 4 Birr and 2/5 of a Birr.
2/5 of a Birr = 40 cents. So each pet gets 4 Birr 40 cents = 22/5 Birr.
A number like 22/5 is a rational number.

screens.title: Introduction
paras: You already know natural numbers, whole numbers and integers.
In this unit you meet a set that contains them all. It is called the rational numbers.

screens.title: Where does each number live?
items: Counting starts at 1, so 0 is whole but not natural.
−4 is negative. Whole numbers are never negative, but integers can be.
screens.text: Put each number in the FIRST set it belongs to. Natural numbers come first, then whole numbers, then integers.
screens.why:
Natural numbers: 1, 2, 3, …
Whole numbers: add 0, so 0, 1, 2, 3, …
Integers: add the negatives, so …, −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, …
Each set holds the one before it. The rational numbers will hold them all.

screens.title: Definition 1.1
defs: A number that can be written as a/b, where a and b are integers and b ≠ 0.

screens.title: Which set is biggest?
screens.text: Number sets: which of these sets includes the other two?
screens.why:
Natural numbers are 1, 2, 3, …
Whole numbers are the natural numbers plus 0.
Integers are the whole numbers plus the negatives −1, −2, …
So the integers include both other sets. Answer: Integers.
screens.clue: Which set also has the negative numbers?

screens.title: Spot the rational numbers
screens.text: Rational numbers: tap every number that can be written as a/b with b ≠ 0.
screens.why:
3/4 is already a/b with b = 4.
−8/2 has b = 2, so it is rational (it equals −4).
0 = 0/1 and 5 = 5/1.
7/0 has b = 0. Dividing by 0 is not allowed, so it is not rational.
screens.clue: Check the bottom number. It must not be 0.

screens.text: Rational numbers: true or false? 22/5 is a rational number.
screens.why:
A rational number is a/b with integers a, b and b ≠ 0.
Here a = 22 and b = 5. Both are integers.
b = 5 is not 0.
So 22/5 is rational: true.
screens.clue: Are the top and bottom both integers?

screens.title: Solomon's toys
screens.ask: Sharing money: 22 Birr shared equally by 5 pets gives ___ Birr each.
screens.why:
Share means divide: 22 ÷ 5.
22 ÷ 5 = 4 remainder 2, so 22/5 = 4 2/5.
2/5 = 0.40, so each pet gets 4.40 Birr.
Check: 5 × 4.40 = 22.
screens.worked:
22 ÷ 5 = 4 remainder 2.
So 22/5 = 4 2/5.
2/5 = 0.40, so 4 2/5 = 4.40.
Each pet gets 4.40 Birr (4 Birr 40 cents).

screens.text: Number sets: simplify first. Which of these are whole numbers?
screens.why:
18/6 = 18 ÷ 6 = 3. 3 is whole.
7/3 = 2 1/3. It is not an integer, so it is not whole.
−12/4 = −3. It is an integer but negative, so it is not whole.
0/9 = 0. 0 is whole.
Answer: 18/6 and 0/9.
screens.clue: Divide the top by the bottom. Whole numbers are 0, 1, 2, …

items.text: Number sets: which number is whole but NOT natural?
items.why:
Natural numbers start at 1: 1, 2, 3, …
Whole numbers add 0: 0, 1, 2, …
So 0 is the only whole number that is not natural.
1 and 10 are natural; −1 is not whole at all.

items.text: Number sets: which number is an integer but NOT a whole number?
items.why:
Whole numbers are 0, 1, 2, … They are never negative.
Integers also include −1, −2, −3, …
−3 is an integer and it is negative, so it is not whole.
0 and 3 are whole; 1/2 is not an integer.

items.text: Number sets: which set of numbers includes the other two sets?
items.why:
Every natural number is a whole number.
Every whole number is an integer.
So ℕ ⊂ W ⊂ ℤ: the integers include the other two.
Answer: Integers.

items.ask: Sharing money: Solomon has 22 Birr for 5 pets. Each pet gets ___ Birr.
items.why:
3 cats + 2 dogs = 5 pets.
22 ÷ 5 = 4 remainder 2, so 22/5 = 4 2/5 Birr.
2/5 Birr = 40 cents.
Each pet gets 4.40 Birr (4 Birr 40 cents).

test.text: Definition of a rational number: a/b where a and b are integers and …
test.why:
A rational number is a/b with a and b integers.
The bottom number b divides the top.
Dividing by 0 has no meaning, so b ≠ 0.
a can be 0 (0/5 = 0), and a can be bigger or smaller than b.

test.text: Rational numbers: true or false? −6 is a rational number.
test.why:
Any integer n can be written n/1.
−6 = −6/1.
−6 and 1 are integers and 1 ≠ 0.
So −6 is rational: true.

test.text: Rational numbers: true or false? 5/0 is a rational number.
test.why:
A rational number needs a/b with b ≠ 0.
Here b = 0.
Dividing by 0 is not allowed.
So 5/0 is not rational: false.

test.text: Rational numbers: which number is NOT rational?
test.why:
0/7 = 0, which is rational (7 ≠ 0).
−7 = −7/1 and 0.7 = 7/10 are rational.
7/0 has denominator 0, which is not allowed.
So 7/0 is not rational.

test.ask: Sharing money: three friends share 40 Birr equally. Each gets ___ Birr.
test.why:
Share means divide: 40 ÷ 3.
40 ÷ 3 = 13 remainder 1.
So 40/3 = 13 1/3 Birr (about 13.33 Birr).
Check: 3 × 13 1/3 = 39 + 1 = 40.
